result:
If I could change the world in one single, fundamental way, I would make every human being *radically more curious* and less certain.

Not kinder (though that would follow).  
Not smarter (though that would follow).  
Not more empathetic (though that would follow).

Just… insatiably, uncomfortably, joyfully *curious*, paired with a deep, reflexive humility about how much they don’t know.

Imagine a world where:

- The default response to disagreement is “Huh, that’s interesting. Tell me why you see it that way,” instead of “You’re an idiot.”
- People treated their own beliefs like working hypotheses rather than sacred identity tattoos.
- Curiosity became the main status signal in society instead of wealth, power, or performative certainty.
- Education, politics, social media algorithms, and even religion were all optimized around “How can we make people better at wanting to understand?”

I genuinely believe almost every other problem we have (tribalism, environmental destruction, inequality, mental health crises, technological risk) is downstream of the current human addiction to certainty and belonging over truth-seeking.

So yeah. One change.

Make us a species that falls in love with reality instead of our stories about it.
